fields.title: Polka: the boundary across the screen
fields.summary: Delivery splits into a separate service. The boundary affects the main screen across 340 thousand opens.
fields.decisionPrompt: Where do we draw the boundary? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are the Polka product manager. The delivery service is splitting from the order service—the delivery team has grown to eight people and is tired of shared releases. The architect proposes a boundary. You were invited to the discussion because the decision affects the main screen.
fields.brief/objective: Draw the boundary so the main screen does not depend on delivery availability.
fields.brief/constraints: Two teams are waiting two days each for shared releases. Status changes 4 to 6 times per order.
fields.brief/task: Decide where to draw the boundary and state the cost of the chosen model.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Service boundaries are drawn by reads, not code
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Splitting services means deciding where each screen gets its data. A high-traffic screen must not depend on a neighbor's availability: it reads a snapshot updated by an event. A detail screen, visited an order of magnitude less often, can afford a live source. The question "how fresh does this number need to be" must be answered before talking about databases and calls.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Delivery is a separate service with its own database. The order stores the delivery ID. Delivery status is read via an inter-service call upon display.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Order card on the main screen — 340k opens per day. Order list — 90k. Tracking screen — 60k.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "Inter-service call is 20–40 ms normally. If delivery is unavailable, the order card will not show status. Alternative — the order stores a status snapshot updated by an event: zero reads, but status may lag by seconds."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Change 4–6 times per order, usually at intervals of tens of minutes. Simultaneous active orders peak at up to 3 thousand.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: As proposed: inter-service call upon display
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: As proposed: inter-service call upon display. Two weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: status is always up-to-date. 490 thousand additional inter-service calls per day. When delivery is unavailable, the main screen shows orders without status — 70 minutes over half a year. Simple model, easy to understand.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Status snapshot in the order, updated by event
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Status snapshot in the order, updated by event. Three weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: zero read calls, main screen does not depend on delivery. Status lags by seconds after a change. When delivery is unavailable, the last known status is shown — looks normal to the user. Data duplication requires handling out-of-sync states.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Do not split, keep in a single service
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Do not split, keep in a single service. Zero weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: no inter-service problems. Two teams still wait 2 days for each other per release — which is the root cause of the split. In a year, the situation will worsen.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Split, snapshot in order, but tracking screen reads delivery directly
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Split, snapshot in order, but tracking screen reads delivery directly. Three weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: high-traffic screens are fast and independent, the detailed tracking screen is always up-to-date. Two access models instead of one — slightly more complex. 60 thousand calls instead of 490 thousand.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not see product substance in the service boundary
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not connect the split to team autonomy
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not design behavior for partial system unavailability
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Inter-service backward compatibility is ignored when choosing the boundary
